land.text: the Saar, 'disentangled from the Allied zones of occupation' by France on 16 February 1946, with 109 municipalities of the Prussian Rhine Province added from 20 July 1946
Saarland, which 'joined the Federal Republic of Germany as a state on 1 January 1957'

successors.note: Economic union with France lasted until 6 July 1959 (Saar (protectorate) page).

capitals.name: Saarbrücken
capitals.note: The Saarland page names Saarbrücken the state capital and largest city; the protectorate page names no capital. Coordinates are the city's.

rulers.name: Johannes Hoffmann (CVP), head of government
rulers.title: Minister-President
rulers.note: 1947 to 1952 and again 1952 to 1955; first elections 5 October 1947. The French High Commissioner Gilbert Grandval held office from 10 January 1948 to 5 March 1952, then headed the diplomatic mission to 8 July 1955; de Carbonnel then to 27 October 1956.

correction.text: the Saar around Saarbrücken in February 1946, enlarged on 20 July 1946 by 109 municipalities of the Prussian Rhine Province; today's Saarland (2,571.52 km2) stands in for the protectorate after the later exchanges of villages

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The protectorate page leaves its area and population blank, so no infobox comparison is possible; today's Saarland, 2,571.52 km2 in the infobox of the Saarland page, is the best proxy. The page says 61 municipalities were later returned to Germany and 13 more ceded to the Saar between 8 June 1947 and 1949 without naming them, so the exact line is unverified.

region.text: the Saar around Saarbrücken, the part of the French zone cut out in February 1946; the pages give no boundary, so a 30 km radius stands in

ledger.note: 16 February 1946: France separates the Saar from the Allied zones. 'On 16 February 1946, France disentangled the Saar from the Allied zones of occupation'; a 'French protectorate and a disputed territory separated from Germany', with France handling defence and foreign affairs. The Allied-occupied Germany page gives the same date.

region.text: the Saar around Saarbrücken, the part of the French zone cut out in February 1946; the pages give no boundary, so a 30 km radius stands in

ledger.note: 16 February 1946: the Saar becomes a French protectorate. 'On 16 February 1946, France disentangled the Saar from the Allied zones of occupation'; the page calls it 'a French protectorate and a disputed territory separated from Germany', with France 'responsible for defence and foreign affairs'. Mirror of the vassal_start in french-fourth-republic; added by the eu-22-x reviewer.

region.text: 109 municipalities of the Prussian Rhine Province in the French zone; named here as Saarland less the core, which is a reading

ledger.note: 20 July 1946: 109 municipalities are added to the Saar. 'With effect from 20 July 1946, 109 municipalities' of the Prussian Rhine Province in the French zone were added to the protectorate.

region.text: 13 Palatine municipalities along the Saar's border

ledger.note: From 8 June 1947 to 1949: 13 more municipalities are ceded to the Saar by Rhineland-Palatinate. The page says '13 other municipalities were ceded to the Saar Protectorate between 8 June 1947 and 1949' and that 61 municipalities returned to Germany through redeployments (no date); too small for the grid.

15 December 1947: the Saar is constituted as the Saarland. 'On 15 December 1947 the Saar was constituted by its constitution as the Saarland' (in force two days later); the Saarland page says it 'became the Saar Protectorate on 17 December 1947', which differs from the protectorate page's February 1946.

region.text: Saarland, to the Federal Republic of Germany

ledger.note: 1 January 1957: the protectorate ends as the Saar 'became a state of West Germany (as Saarland) on 1 January 1957'. Mirror of the vassal_end in french-fourth-republic; added by the eu-22-x reviewer.

region.text: Saarland, to the Federal Republic of Germany

ledger.note: 1 January 1957: the Saar joins West Germany. The Saar Treaty of 27 October 1956 'established that Saarland should be allowed to become a state of West Germany', after the 23 October 1955 referendum rejected the Saar Statute by 67.7% to 32.3% (turnout 96.5%). Saarland 'joined the Federal Republic of Germany as a state on 1 January 1957'.

certainty.note: Municipal boundaries fixed by decree (20 July 1946) and exchanged in 1947-49; the pages give no coordinates, so the cells follow today's Saarland border.

sources.title: Saar (protectorate)
sources.note: Whole dossier: 16 February 1946, 20 July 1946 municipalities, constitution, customs union 1948, referendum 1955, Saar Treaty 1956, accession 1 January 1957; area blank.

sources.note: Corroborates 16 February 1946; opened for the allied-occupied-germany dossier.

notes: Requested as a counterpart by eu-22-a. The History of Saarland page did not load (url_not_found). French dossier (eu-22-a) records a vassal_start for the Saar in February 1946; its end is 1 January 1957 and the economic union ended on 6 July 1959 (Saar (protectorate) page). The page also says Kehl was 'directly annexed to France in 1945 and returned to Germany in 1953': a French annexation outside the Saar, a gap for the French dossier. Not settled: the protectorate's area and population (blank on the page), the names and dates of the 61 returned municipalities, the pre-1946 Saar boundary (the core is a 30 km radius), the month of the first government. Gazetteer: Saarland is Natural Earth's admin1; the core is a radius around Saarbrücken.
